name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo loop (Drei Zinnen)
region: Dolomiti di Sesto / Auronzo di Cadore, Belluno
why: The most famous walk of the Dolomites: all the way round the three rock towers, from their bright south walls to the north faces everyone knows, on wide paths with three huts on the way.
book: Free path. By car: toll road from Misurina to Rifugio Auronzo, parking booked online in advance since 2025 (40 EUR a car in 2026). Or the summer shuttle bus from Dobbiaco or Misurina. Huts open roughly mid-June to late September.
water: No streams worth trusting: fill up at Rifugio Auronzo. Rifugio Lavaredo, Locatelli and Malga Langalm sell drinks and food.
dangers: Afternoon thunderstorms in July and August: you are on open ground at 2,300-2,450 m with no shelter between the huts.
Snow on the north side and on Forcella Lavaredo until late June.
Very crowded from 10:00 in summer: start early.
turnaround: If thunder starts before Forcella Lavaredo, go back to Auronzo the way you came; after the pass, shelter at Rifugio Locatelli.

points.name: Rifugio Auronzo
points.note: 2,320 m, end of the toll road and of the bus. Walk east on the flat gravel road (path 101) under the south walls.

points.name: Rifugio Lavaredo
points.note: 2,344 m, after 30 minutes. Small hut with a terrace below the Cima Piccola; the path then climbs to the pass.

points.name: Forcella Lavaredo
points.note: 2,454 m, the highest point. The north faces of the Tre Cime appear on the left, Monte Paterno on the right.

points.name: Rifugio Locatelli
points.note: 2,405 m, the classic view of the three north faces straight across the valley. Lunch here, then take path 105 west.

points.name: Malga Langalm
points.note: 2,283 m, a small pasture hut by two little lakes. From here the path climbs gently back to Rifugio Auronzo in 45 minutes.
